newsitem.title: USA: Maverick Airways to restructure, suspend service.
newsitem.headline: Maverick Airways to restructure, suspend service.

text.p: Maverick Airways said it would suspend scheduled service this week for an undetermined period, pending a restructuring of its business plan.

The company said the board's decision was made in light of the rapidly changing regional air service environment in the Rocky Mountains, and as part of Maverick's second round of direct placement financing.
The decision was unrelated to government action involving other regional airlines' maintenance activities, it said.
It was "in view of the marginal advance bookings and lack of revenue traffic at this time," according to a company statement for employees.
Maverick also said its founder and president Cody Diekroeger was asked to submit his resignation.
Alan Willis, vice president of operations, was named interim president, the carrier said.
Maverick said it was working closely with the Federal Aviation Administration and it would likely have charter flights during the summer pending approval.
The carrier said its reservations center would stay open to help protect passengers and accept reservations when scheduled operations resume later this year.
Scheduled westbound service between Denver International Airport, Steamboat Springs and Grand Junction would end on Monday night, the company said.
Eastbound service back to Denver would end on Tuesday morning, it said.
Maverick said its board was considering several options, including resumption of scheduled service, seasonal service, or numerous charter opportunities.
The company said its goal was to resume scheduled operations in late autumn or early winter.
